chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer in Mecca, so he said: 'Complete it (the full four rak'ahs), and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam
key_terms.أَتِمَّ: Complete (the prayer, i.e., pray four rak'ahs)
key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening the prayer (performing two rak'ahs instead of four)
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city where the Kaaba is located

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to shorten prayer in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling of *qasr* (shortening prayer) in Mecca, distinguishing between obligation and recommendation. He affirms that while completing the full four rak'ahs is not strictly wajib, it is mustahabb based on his personal preference, reflecting the scholarly view that the Prophet's practice in Mecca was a voluntary act of worship rather than a binding legal requirement. This highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding prayers in the two holy sanctuaries.
